segments: And five hundred horsemen fell from a high crag in the night and died.
These things took place in the month of Ab of the year 1541
of the Greeks
(1230 of our Lord).
And because the lord of Arzan al-Rum,
who was the cousin of Sultan Ala al-Din and his brother-in-law,
had acted treacherously against the Sultan
and made an alliance with the Khwarazmians,
and used to march before them in battle,
he too was taken prisoner.
And the Sultan went with al-Ashraf against Arzan al-Rum,
and they attacked it fiercely.
And after the people inside made the Sultan swear an oath
that they would not kill their lord,
the one who had been imprisoned,
they surrendered the city [to him].
Now there was in it the sister of the lord of Arzan al-Rum,
the very one whom for a long time the Sultan had desired to take in marriage,
and her brother would not consent.
And when the Sultan took her,
he rejoiced in her more than in all the victory that he had achieved.
However, after a little while,
when she asked of the Sultan to release her brother from bonds,
he became angry with her and put her to death;
and he also sent her brother and had him drowned in the sea.
And after the defeat of the Khwarazmians,
al-Ashraf went to Khilat to repair its breaches and to settle it;
and the Sultan sent with him a thousand horsemen, along with lavish gifts.
And the Sultan himself also returned to his own country.
Jalal al-Din the Khwarazmshah, however, took his household and went and stayed in Khoy, a city of Azerbaijan.
And he sent Taqi al-Din, the brother of al-Ashraf, while bound in fetters, as a present to the Caliph in Baghdad;
and that Caliph released him and sent him with honor to al-Ashraf.
Then al-Ashraf sent an envoy to the Khwarazmshah and said to him:
"You came and ruined our lands, and killed and plundered, when we had not offended against you.
And if, on account of Hajib Ali who devastated a portion of your country, you wished to take vengeance upon us,
behold, he was killed in battle and was repaid according to his deeds.
And we ask of you to relinquish the territory that you took tyrannically,
and make peace with us."
The Khwarazmshah, however, made light of him and would not make peace.
So al-Ashraf left and went to Mesopotamia,
while al-Kamil was in Egypt.
And Mujir al-Din Yaqub, the brother of al-Ashraf, remained a prisoner with the Khwarazmshah.
